title: Full-Key Unpredictability in the CTR-DRBG Bound
summary: The analysis uses only prefix unpredictability; whether full-key unpredictability yields a tighter CTR-DRBG bound for AES-192 and AES-256 remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the CTR-DRBG security analysis, the bound contains a term $pq/2^n$ because it uses only the unpredictability of the $n$-bit prefix of each CTR key rather than that of the entire $k$-bit key. Determine whether exploiting unpredictability of the entire key can replace $pq/2^n$ with $pq/2^k$, yielding a better bound when the underlying block cipher is AES-192 or AES-256.

scope.domain: Provable security analysis of the NIST CTR-DRBG construction using a block cipher.
parameters: p and q, quantities appearing in the security bound
n, length of the considered key prefix
k, length of the entire CTR key
AES-192 or AES-256, underlying block-cipher variants
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether exploiting unpredictability of the entire key can replace the existing term with pq/2^k and yield a better bound for AES-192 or AES-256.

progress.summary: The source identifies the existing bound term as an artifact of considering only the n-bit prefix and suggests that full-key unpredictability could improve it. The improvement is left open for AES-192 and AES-256.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., Security Analysis of NIST CTR-DRBG
